In [[geometric topology]], a branch of mathematics, a '''crumpled cube''' is any space in [[Euclidean space|'''R'''<sup>3</sup>]] [[homeomorphic]] to a [[n-sphere|2-sphere]] together with its [[interior (topology)|interior]].<ref name="Martin65">{{cite journal | last1 = Martin | first1 = Joseph | year = 1966 | title = The sum of two crumpled cubes | url = https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.mmj/1028999538 | journal = [[Michigan Mathematical Journal]] | volume = 13 | issue = 2| pages = 147–151 | doi=10.1307/mmj/1028999538| doi-access = free }} {{open access}}</ref> Lininger showed in 1965 that the [[union (set theory)|union]] of a crumpled cube and an [[ball (mathematics)|open 3-ball]] glued along their [[boundary (topology)|boundaries]] is a 3-sphere.<ref name="Lininger1965">{{cite journal | last1=Lininger | first1=Lloyd L. | title=Some results on crumpled cubes | jstor=1993977 | mr=0178460  | year=1965 | journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] | issn=0002-9947 | volume=118 | pages=534–549 | doi=10.2307/1993977| doi-access=free }} {{open access}}</ref>
